resolvedFindings: Transitive YAML parser imports blocked browser startup. Split UI-safe template functions and build API constants from server-side parsing; static browser module graph and real Chrome now pass.
A delayed native dialog close event could invalidate a newly opened World read. Guard close handling by actual dialog state; delayed-event regression and rapid browser reopen pass.

Projection display names used generic JSON filenames instead of authored titles. World and Build use projection.title; title property edits update both while ordinary documents keep their parser titles.
Runtime projections preserve their own UUIDs and core source trace; projections without runtime mappings cannot bypass checks via explicit actor fields.
Projection source/asset registration and template locks are validated for selective export and import; full backup still preserves damaged authored text.
Generic image fields accept available image resources including GIF; only Scene2D runtime image fields apply Godot format and size restrictions.

earlierAttempts.outcome: Smoke polling asserted HTTP 200 while a live transaction correctly fenced readers; polling now retries only known transient conflicts.
Smoke reached real runtime success, then clicked the old page during reload; now awaits a new navigation time origin and loaded object list.
Linux /proc read raced process reaping (ESRCH). Test now accepts ENOENT/ESRCH while still requiring any observable descendant to be dead.
Passed before the final authored-title mapping adjustment; final check.log verifies the resulting sources.

limits: No packaged Tauri window or Android device validation in this round; native storage helper interoperability is not device UI acceptance.
Headless smoke verifies movement and state; graphical runtime preview was not repeated.
Only Scene2D-mapped projections execute. RPG level/health/interactable and visual-novel/literature/drama fields remain design data, without automatic combat, AI or narrative execution.
Saved templates are self-contained snapshots; no automatic template upgrades or third-party package installer.
Non-image configuration uses existing property edits. Source identity/template lock/image edits require source and registration consistency; no general mixed transaction editor.
No new version, installation, commit or push. Unsaved form drafts remain in page memory.
